title: Sealtest Variety Theater
paragraphs: A late-1940s variety and comedy program hosted by Dorothy Lamour, combining sketches, music, celebrity guests, and an increasing emphasis on comedy during its run.
NBC Thursday-night comedy-musical variety program hosted by Dorothy Lamour and sponsored by Sealtest.
The run breaks into several distinct periods: Sealtest Variety Theater NBC run (September 9, 1948 to July 7, 1949) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Dorothy Lamour (performer), Glenhall Taylor (director and performer), Henry Russell and His Orchestra (performer), Howard Harris (writer), Sid Zelinka (writer), The Crew Chiefs (performer), and John Laing (announcer).
Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] and [[org|org.f8dbaeb1115d17fa|KPRC]].

The stories often return to celebrity musical variety, comedy sketches and parody, popular music performance, Hollywood and radio guest stars, sponsored network variety radio, and live remote broadcasting.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Live remote from the Shamrock Hotel, Front and Center predecessor to Sealtest Variety Theater, Dorothy Lamour hosts NBC Sealtest Variety Theater, and Later-run comedy emphasis.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]], [[show|screen-directors-playhouse|Screen Directors Playhouse]], [[show|duffys-tavern|Duffy's Tavern]], [[show|the-railroad-hour|The Railroad Hour]], and [[show|fibber-mcgee-and-molly|Fibber McGee and Molly]].
